gap: No study isolates whether the accuracy gain from context-augmented KG supervision comes from the coherence of the same-passage supporting triples or merely from the additional context tokens those triples introduce.

evidence.quote: all four models are initialized from the same base model and trained using the same fine-tuning configuration, LoRA setup, optimizer, sequence length, batch size, number of epochs, and learning-rate schedule.

Holding the number of triples fixed and replacing every triple that is not on the chain with material from an unrelated entity changes answer accuracy by +0.003 F1, while removing the chain costs most of what the graph was worth.

why_unaddressed: The one study that runs the training-time contrast (arxiv:2609.12230) matches the number of QA items, every hyperparameter, the optimizer and the schedule, but each CG item contains additional supporting triples, so the context-augmented arm consumes more context tokens per example; no random-distractor or unrelated-entity control arm was run, and its stated limitations do not mention this confound. The one study that did run a matched context/distractor swap (arxiv:2609.10237) held the triple count fixed at inference time over 125 questions with a frozen LLM and never fine-tuned, so its null cannot settle the training-time question.
research_question: At a fixed context-token budget and a fixed number of optimization steps, does replacing same-passage supporting triples with random or unrelated-entity triples reduce the multi-hop accuracy gain from fine-tuning?
potential_experiment: Run a three-arm fine-tuning comparison at a strictly matched context-token budget and identical optimizer steps: (i) target triple/path only, padded to the budget; (ii) target plus same-passage supporting triples; (iii) target plus an equal number of randomly sampled or unrelated-entity triples. Add a triple-order-shuffled arm to neutralise serialization. Report EM/F1 by hop depth with confidence intervals, using the same base model and hyperparameters across arms.
verification_required: The appendix of arxiv:2609.12230 was not read, so it is not yet confirmed that no token-matched or random-distractor ablation is reported there; a full-appendices read is required. Re-run a literature search when the paper budget resets, targeting token-matched context ablations and distractor-context controls in knowledge-grounded fine-tuning.
